paper_title: HeLIOS: The Superfluid Helium Ultralight Dark Matter Detector
suggested_experiment_name: Eot-Wash (existing bound shown in HeLIOS vector UDM plot)
notes: Prototype superfluid helium optomechanical detector presenting projected sensitivities (after 1 hour integration) for both scalar UDM (coupling to electron mass d_me, ScalarElectron) and vector UDM (gB-L, VectorBL). These are projections, not measured limits. The paper covers two coupling types; per hint and exclusion plot the vector channel is gB-L (VectorBL). Mass range ~1-10 peV (1e-12 to 1e-11 eV), Compton freq ~0.3-10 kHz. Vector coupling axis spans ~1e-26 to 1e-16. No numerical table of (mass, coupling) exclusion points is provided; only plotted projection curves. Local DM density 0.4 GeV/cm^3 stated. | Vision: Right panel of Fig.1 shows vector UDM g_BL vs mass [peV]. The lower boundary traced corresponds to the lowest existing constraint envelope (Eot-Wash / LIGO-Virgo) bounding the excluded region from below. HeLIOS projected sensitivities (red) lie above. Axis multiplier and log scale read per calibration. Values approximate due to overlapping shaded regions. | CV axis calibration: y-max corrected 1e+07->6.35213e-05; | Calibration: No calibration needed | Auto-corrected masses: 1/(eV→MHz) i.e. MHz→eV inverse (×2.418e+08, rule=argmin|log10(median*f)-log10(anchor=1.0e-03)|)
